text:
[verdict]
In the 50 retrieved episodes where the tape looked like this, SPY and its analogs produced a median 5-session return of -0.1%, with outcomes split almost evenly between gains and losses. The single number to anchor on is the 10th percentile of that distribution: -2.39%. This is a historical conditional distribution describing what happened next in similar states, not a forecast of what will happen over the next five sessions.

[state]
The current state as of 2026-09-18 is defined by three dominant features that pull specific historical episodes into the neighborhood. First, the 20-session dollar-volume regime z-score (dv20z) sits at -1.985, indicating unusually thin liquidity. Second, WTI crude change over 20 days (oilChg20) is 19.24%, a sharp energy move. Third, 20-session realised volatility (vol20) is compressed at 9.16%. These features carry heavy weight in the retrieval engine's name group (30% of the distance metric) and macro group (20%). The combination of low volume, an oil shock, and suppressed volatility retrieves a set of 50 analogs spanning 28 distinct sessions and 22 distinct symbols from 2016-12-14 to 2026-09-08. The closest match is IWM on 2026-09-08 at a distance of 0.2997, followed by UUP on the same date at 0.3029, and SPY itself on 2026-09-03 at 0.3101.

[history]
Over the 5-session horizon, the 50 analogs produced a mean return of -0.03% and a median of -0.1%. The standard deviation was 2.14%. The distribution carries a slight positive skew of 0.51, meaning the upside tail is somewhat fatter than the downside. Exactly 48% of the analogs finished above zero, while 52% finished below it. The 10th percentile was -2.39% and the 90th percentile was 3.29%. The absolute worst outcome was -5.12% and the best was 6.88%.

The bad tail is dominated by recent broad-market ETF sessions. The closest analog, IWM on 2026-09-08, returned -2.98%. SPY on 2026-09-03 returned -1.15%, and DIA on 2026-09-02 returned -1.86%. JPM on 2026-09-04 contributed a -2.37% forward return. Conversely, the upside tail includes SPY on 2025-06-20, which returned 3.47%, and BAC on 2026-08-31, which returned 1.24%. The histogram shows the bulk of outcomes clustered between -1.37% and 1.13%, with the -0.37% midpoint bin holding the largest share at 12%.

[tails]
Path risk matters because a trade can end near flat while being un-holdable along the way. Across the 50 analogs, the median max adverse excursion was -1.05%. At the 25th percentile, the path dipped -1.98% before recovering, and at the 10th percentile, the max adverse excursion reached -3.1%. On the upside, the median max favourable excursion was 0.99%, the 75th percentile was 1.89%, and the 90th percentile was 3.52%. The reward-to-risk ratio based on these excursions is 0.94.

Regarding drawdown breaches during the 5-session path, the probability of breaching a 5% drawdown was 4%. The probability of breaching a 10%, 15%, or 20% drawdown was 0% across all 50 retrieved episodes.

[stress]
When conditioned on specific stress regimes, the baseline picture changes materially. The 2020-02/03 liquidity crash scenario is the most severe. Using 48 analogs, the median 5-session forward return was -4.61%, a delta of -4.51% versus the baseline. The 10th percentile plunged to -11.63%, and the probability of falling below -10% was 16.7%. The median max adverse excursion was -8.46%, and the probability of breaching a 10% drawdown was 41.7%. Caveat: Central-bank backstops arrived inside the window, so the realised rebound is baked into the forward returns. It is a sample of one regime, not a forecast of the next one.

The 2025-04 tariff shock scenario used 26 analogs and produced a median return of -0.92% (delta of -0.82%), but the 10th percentile was -11.26%. The probability of falling below -10% was 15.4%, and the probability of breaching a 10% drawdown was 23.1%. Caveat: Policy reversals inside the window make the tail of the distribution asymmetric in a way that is specific to that episode.

The 2022 inflation / rate bear scenario (50 analogs) yielded a median return of -2.09% (delta of -1.99%) and a 10th percentile of -5.01%. Caveat: A nine-month window means the per-date cap of 2 analogs samples it repeatedly; treat it as a regime description, not 50 independent events.

The 2018-Q4 tightening scare (50 analogs) produced a median of -1.09% (delta of -0.99%) and a 10th percentile of -4.75%. Caveat: Ended with a policy pivot in January 2019, which flatters the forward returns of late-window analogs.

The 2024-08-05 carry unwind (36 analogs) had a median of -0.49% (delta of -0.39%) and a 10th percentile of -4.04%. Caveat: Reversal was almost as fast as the drawdown, so H-day forward returns look benign even though the intra-horizon excursion did not.

The 2023-03 regional bank stress (36 analogs) actually produced a positive median of 1.41% (delta of 1.51%). Caveat: Very short window; the analog set will be dominated by a handful of sessions.

Shock scenarios showed smaller deviations. A Volatility spike (+2 sigma VIX) shifted the median by -0.1% to -0.2%. A Liquidity air pocket shifted it by -0.03% to -0.13%. An Earnings release day shifted it by -0.69% to -0.79%. An FOMC decision day shifted it by -0.01% to -0.11%. A Crypto drawdown contagion shifted it positively by 0.87% to 0.77%. A China ADR de-rating shifted it by 0.26% to 0.16%. A Policy-rate path re-pricing shifted it by 0.17% to 0.07%. Each shock carries its own caveat regarding mean-reversion timing, proxy limitations, event noise, or structural risks not captured in price features. No scenarios were skipped.

[limits]
This analysis has concrete limits. The engine's own validation states: "Analog retrieval hits its coverage target out of sample and its width tracks each instrument's own volatility, but it is NOT sharper than a same-name unconditional band at matched coverage, and its raw PIT distribution fails a uniformity test. It is a stress-testing and provenance instrument, not an alpha source." Specifically, the conformal analog coverage is 80.8% with a width of 10.4%, while the unconditional same-name benchmark achieves 82.4% coverage with a narrower width of 10.12%. At matched coverage, the analog is 7.6% less sharp. The directional hit rate is 50.1%, and the PIT chi-square statistic of 208.6 vastly exceeds the 5% critical value of 16.92. The retrieval spans 2513 sessions and 71 symbols, using 25 metric features, with prices sourced keyless from api.stockanalysis.com.

If traded via the verified tokenised wrapper SPYG_USDT on Gate.io spot v4, the status is measured. The reference cash market is shut for 81.4% of the week, and 60.93% of the wrapper's own realised hourly movement landed in those closed hours. It is classified as a fair tracker with a return correlation of 0.9358 and a tracking error of 25 bp/day. The premium band over the underlying's raw close is -0.08% to 0.31%, and the spread is 11.95 bps. Caveat: Measured on Gate.io spot v4 (public, keyless). A fair tracker is not the underlying—at 25 bp/day of tracking error the wrapper carries its own idiosyncratic risk, and the premium band means the exit price can differ from the reference close the analog distribution is built on. Nothing here feeds the retrieval engine, the conformal scale or any validation figure.

For sizing purposes, the closed-session return layer observed 4 weekend blocks. The median weekend block return was -0.127%, the 10th percentile was -0.6367%, and the standard deviation was 0.5694%. The median intra-weekend adverse excursion was -0.3225%. Zero percent of these specific weekend blocks breached the 5% drawdown threshold. These are wrapper returns measured while the reference market was shut and NOT the retrieved outcome distribution above, which is built on 5x24 daily sessions.
